hits.text: Positions 1–12 are Or7a + ORCO, Or19a + ORCO, Or42a + ORCO, Or98a + ORCO, Or22a + ORCO, Or67a + ORCO, Or67b + ORCO, Or59b + ORCO, Or85b + ORCO, Or35a + ORCO, ORCO only and blank. F0 contains five reads over 0–48 s; F1 contains fifteen reads over 0–168 s, both at 12 s intervals. Each acquisition starts its own clock. Results defines the endpoint correction and VUAA1-reference normalization.

Cross-platform similarity is not specific to matched constructs: D2 gives r = 0.9719 with Or85b and 0.9671 with Or98a, and D3 exceeds its strongest off-diagonal match by only 0.0055. D2 and D3 remain positive after omitting the first point (r = 0.970 and 0.904), whereas restoring original record 19 changes D4 from +0.948 to −0.290. The original series spans 69.186 s, while the replacement lacks a verified timestamp. Control subtraction preserves some shared trends, but preceding hardware-medium readings and separate wet-lab DMSO wells are different references. Serial time points do not establish synchronized kinetics, biological replication or receptor-specific activation.

The subsequent F1 -only reanalysis compares four odorants with DoOR consensus minus receptor-specific spontaneous firing rate. Across tuning receptors, Pearson r / Spearman ρ are +0.317 / +0.406 for 2-heptanone, +0.325 / +0.442 for isopentyl acetate, +0.211 / +0.283 for valeric acid, and −0.002 / +0.006 for pentyl acetate. The comparison includes ten receptors per odorant, except the missing Or42a–valeric acid reference (n = 9). Results presents the two comparison figures .
Figure 12 compares all twelve cell conditions. In Test 2, corrected changes are +36.67 pp for Or98a + ORCO, +18.69 pp for ORCO only and −0.11 pp for the blank control.

Figure 14. Test 2 VUAA1-referenced responses, with DMSO set to 0 and VUAA1 to 1 for each construct and one well per condition; Or7a–Or98a coexpress ORCO. Orange cells retain negative ratios; †Or7a has a small VUAA1 reference (2.19 pp), making its ratios particularly sensitive to that reference.

Figure 15. F1 -only odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts (top, pp) and DoOR consensus minus receptor-specific spontaneous firing rate, SFR (bottom, DoOR units). The scales differ between panels. Each experimental condition has one well; all ten tuning OR conditions coexpress ORCO. The grey cell is the missing Or42a–valeric acid DoOR value. The fluorescence contrast compares early and late three-reading means; Experiments gives the calculation . DoOR-derived material: Münch and Galizia, 2016 , CC BY-SA 4.0 .

The odor assays provide time-resolved evidence of VUAA1-associated fluorescence. In Test 2, F0-subtracted VUAA1 changes are +36.67 pp for Or98a + ORCO, +17.52 pp for Or85b + ORCO, +29.46 pp for Or35a + ORCO, and +18.69 pp for ORCO only, compared with −0.11 pp in the blank control. The control maps and retained raw records make these observations inspectable.

For Test 2, we calculate the endpoint change within each acquisition and subtract the F0 change from the F1 change. S is expressed in percentage points (pp). For Or98a + ORCO with VUAA1, +34.09% − (−2.57%) gives +36.67 pp using unrounded values. ORCO only gives +18.69 pp, while the blank control gives −0.11 pp.

Control behavior remains important. In Test 1, the Or35a + ORCO buffer-only well had a 35.25% excursion. In Test 2, all twelve DMSO-control S values lie between −1.79 and −0.31 pp. Or7a + ORCO has a small positive S of +0.40 pp even though its F1 signal falls by 1.47%, because F0 falls further. These examples show why both subtraction components accompany the corrected values.
